material_systems.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer

primer.notes: MUST be applied to MDF cut/routed edges BEFORE any latex product. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.1 and §4.1.

material_systems.notes: Edge-only application. Step 1 of MDF two-step prime process. Wainscot panels have routed profiles and cut edges at frame joints — all must be sealed.

material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF

primer.notes: Applied to MDF face surfaces AFTER edge sealing with shellac/oil-based. Builds film, levels surface. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime.

material_systems.notes: Step 2 of MDF two-step prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for FJP/Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare FJP. Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.2 and §4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for FJP wainscot.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut, maple). Per Millwork Doctrine §4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood wainscot substrates.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Wood Primer for Softwood

primer.notes: Standard primer-sealer for bare softwood wainscot panels. Seals and provides tooth for finish coat.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Reuse from SF_WINDOW_INT_NC. Brief proposed SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_STANDARD_WAINSCOT but existing SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC covers the same product category — REUSE OVER CREATION.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Good for wainscot in rooms with limited natural light where yellowing is a concern. Same system as trim, window, and riser specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate (FFD §4.1). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling — critical for large flat wainscot panels where brush marks are highly visible. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Same system as trim, window, and riser specs.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush/roll typically requires 3+ coats per FFD §15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as trim, window, and riser specs.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Wainscot panel primer coverage. SF measured directly from PaintScope input — no conversion needed. MDF edges may absorb more sealer. Raised panel 3D profiles add ~10% surface area over measured wall SF.
assumptions: Single coat primer system (except MDF two-step: edge seal + face prime)
Wainscot SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING

coverage_profiles.notes: Wainscot panel finish coat coverage on primed smooth surface. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage. Raised panel may consume ~10% more material due to increased surface area from 3D profile. Spray method: add 20-30% waste for overspray around frame detail.
assumptions: Raised panel 3D profile adds ~10% to effective surface area

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.usage: Floor protection runners at base of wainscot work area
consumables.notes: Runner-style for wainscot base perimeter. Wainscot is low to floor — drips from brush/spray and sanding dust are primary concerns.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall masking above cap rail line (spray only), general edge masking
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Wall masking required only for spray application method.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12-inch)
consumables.usage: Wall surface masking above cap rail line (spray only)
consumables.notes: Paper + tape system for wall protection above cap rail during spray application. 12-inch width adequate for overspray drift from wainscot-height work.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer sanding for bare substrates, factory primer scuff
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial bare wood sanding and factory primer scuff. Hand sanding or pad sanding.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD §15.4.1).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD §15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable. Rigid block critical for flat panel surfaces to avoid creating waves.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for wainscot panel faces, frame detail, and cutting-in
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for flat panel faces and frame detail. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for wainscot panel spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for wainscot panel work. Broad pass for flat panels, fine detail for frame profiles.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~30 SF of wainscot. Use before every coat.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Panel-to-rail joints, panel-to-stile joints, wainscot-to-wall junction
consumables.notes: Three joint types: (1) panel-to-rail (horizontal internal), (2) panel-to-stile (vertical internal), (3) wainscot-to-wall junction (perimeter). Internal joint density varies by wainscot_type — raised_panel has more joints than flat_panel.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes, minor defects on wainscot panels and frame members
consumables.notes: Lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth. One quart per ~100 SF of wainscot assembly.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at base of wainscot work area
floor_perimeter.condition: ALWAYS — wainscot is low to floor, drip and dust protection mandatory.

wall_adjacent.description: Paper masking above cap rail line to protect wall from overspray

required_inputs.purpose: Floor protection area at wainscot work zone
Wall masking LF above cap rail (spray only)

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: MDF two-step prime: shellac edge seal MUST precede latex face prime
compatibility_rules.notes: SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC on edges first, then SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX on faces. Never reverse. Water-based products on raw MDF edges cause irreversible fiber swelling.

risk_notes.topic: MDF fiber swelling on routed edges
risk_notes.risk: Irreversible fiber swelling if water-based product contacts raw MDF cut/routed edges — wainscot panels have extensive routed profiles
risk_notes.mitigation: Always seal MDF edges with shellac/oil-based sealer (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC) before any latex product. Wainscot panels have more routed edge area than simple risers.

risk_notes.risk: Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer on bare FJP
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare FJP wainscot.

risk_notes.risk: Tannin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats on bare hardwood
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK. Required for all bare hardwood wainscot substrates.

risk_notes.risk: Excessive paint buildup in beadboard grooves, losing groove definition
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats on beadboard. Spray preferred — atomized application minimizes groove fill. If brushing, use brush sized to groove width. Avoid over-application.

risk_notes.topic: Brush marks on large flat panel areas
risk_notes.risk: Visible brush marks on large flat panels from overworking waterborne product
risk_notes.mitigation: Waterborne philosophy (FFD §15.3.1): Apply, tip once, walk away. Roll and Tip on flat panels (FFD §15.6). Sand out marks between coats with rigid block (FFD §15.4.1).

risk_notes.risk: Incomplete coverage in raised panel recessed profiles at panel-to-frame transitions
risk_notes.mitigation: Spray technique: field panels first, then HVLP for frame detail. Brush: work panel-to-frame sequence. Check all recessed profiles for holidays during interstage inspection.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths (MDF edge seal, MDF face prime, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood standard). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, SYS_FF_PREMIUM). Any primer can pair with any finish.
material_notes.mdf_two_step_note: MDF requires two-step prime: edge seal with shellac/oil-based (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC), then face prime with latex (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX). Order is mandatory. Wainscot panels have extensive routed profiles creating more edge area than simple trim or risers.
material_notes.coverage_note: Wainscot SF directly from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING — no conversion needed. Raised panel adds ~10% effective surface area over measured wall SF due to 3D profile.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).
material_notes.caulk_joint_types: Three joint types requiring caulk: (1) panel-to-rail (horizontal internal), (2) panel-to-stile (vertical internal), (3) wainscot-to-wall junction (perimeter). Internal joint density varies by wainscot_type.

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with trim/window/riser spec coverage

assumptions.value: ~10% more material consumption for raised panel due to 3D profile
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical raised panel profile depth
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides raised panel surface area multiplier. 10% is conservative estimate for standard profile depths.

assumptions.value: Internal caulk joints per SF varies by wainscot_type
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical wainscot construction
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines internal joint density for wainscot types. Caulk consumption estimated per assembly, not per SF.
